primitives.note: Dragon Practice stacks accumulate permanently (from champion-ability hits and Q kills), have no stated cap or expiry, and directly scale P's onhit-rider damage on Q/W/E plus gate Q's tier1/2/3 unlocks at 25/125/225 stacks and E's extra-bolt count. A 15s damage fight needs an assumed stack trajectory/starting value.
P adds bonus magic damage scaled by current Dragon Practice stacks to every Q hit, every W explosion, and every E bolt, on top of each ability's own damage.
Q's physical damage and P's Q/E bonus damage both scale with critChance x (critDamage-1) even though Q/E are not basic attacks.
At 225+ stacks Q applies a 3s true-damage burn based on target max HP; repeat applications stack damage without refreshing the timer.
The tier-3 burn executes enemy champions once Smolder's own damage (including the burn tick) would drop them below 6.5% max HP.
Each subsequent W explosion against the same target deals 75% of the prior explosion's damage, so repeated hits on one dummy decay.
E is a 1.25s channel that auto-fires up to 5(+stacks) bolts at the nearest/lowest-HP visible enemy and ends immediately if another ability is cast or Smolder is immobilized.

Q tier-2 fires 2(+stacks/125) bolts in a 15deg arc that explode at max range - unclear how many converge on a single dummy. R's 125-unit-wide center sweetspot gives 50% more damage - unclear whether a single stationary dummy is assumed to stand in the center line.
Mana costs (25 flat / 50-70 by rank / 65 flat / 100 flat) against a low base mana pool could cap the achievable cast count inside 15s, especially with W ranking up in cost.

Q's 50%-effectiveness lifesteal and R's self-heal change Smolder's own sustain, not damage dealt to a stationary non-retaliating dummy; in the survival fight they only matter if Smolder himself is attacking (not defending), so a damage-only dummy fight never reads them.

needsBespoke.why: The kit is expressible with infinite-scaling (Dragon Practice) feeding onhit-rider, conditional-damage, dot/execute-or-threshold, and charge-or-channel primitives, provided the simulator can assume a stack trajectory and resolve the tier-1/2/3 stack-gated unlocks as threshold checks on that scaling stack value.

unsettled.question: How many of Q's tier-2 arc bolts (2 + 0.008xstacks, rounded up) can land on a single stationary dummy in a no-geometry damage fight?
options: All bolts are assumed to hit the single target (treat as pure multi-hit damage)
Only one bolt is assumed to reach a single target given the 15deg spread angle
Simulator should just use the base fireball+explosion damage and ignore tier-2 bolts entirely for a single-target dummy

unsettled.question: What Dragon Practice stack count should the 15s damage fight assume Smolder starts with / ramps to, given stacks are uncapped and gate Q's entire tier system (25/125/225) plus scale P's onhit-rider damage on every ability?
options: Start at 0 stacks and only count stacks actually generated by hits during the simulated 15s
Pre-load to a 'typical mid-game' stack count (e.g. enough to be tier 2 or tier 3) to represent a realistic fight state
Pre-load to exactly one threshold (e.g. 225) to showcase the full kit

unsettled.question: Does a single Q cast that lands its fireball, tier-1 explosion, and tier-2 bolts on the same target grant more than one Dragon Practice stack, given W and E explicitly cap themselves to one stack per cast but the sources never state an equivalent cap for Q?
options: Q is capped to one stack per cast per target like W/E (unstated but implied by symmetry)
Q grants one stack per distinct sub-effect (fireball, explosion, each bolt) that connects with the target
Q only grants a stack via its explicit kill-related bin note (in-flight kill / burn kill) and never from merely hitting a living target

unsettled.question: When a Q cast itself grants a Dragon Practice stack (by hitting the target), does that cast's own P onhit-rider bonus damage use the pre-hit stack count or the post-hit (incremented) stack count?
options: Uses stack count before this cast's stack gain (rider computed first, stack added after)
Uses stack count after this cast's stack gain (stack added, then rider computed)

unsettled.question: Does W's 75%-of-previous explosion damage decay against a given target persist across separate W casts for the whole 15s fight, or reset with each new cast (i.e. does 'previous explosion' only refer to earlier explosions within the same cast, which is moot since W only produces one explosion per hit)?
options: Decay is per-target and persists for the whole fight (each W cast's single explosion is 75% of the prior cast's explosion on that same target)
Decay only applies within-cast and effectively never triggers for a single-target dummy since each W cast produces only one explosion on it

proposal: Assume all cooldowns are available at fight start; open with R immediately since it has by far the longest cooldown (100-120s) and will not come off cooldown again within the 15s window.
Follow with W for its glob damage plus the on-champion-hit explosion, then weave in a basic attack.

Cast Q as soon as it is off cooldown and keep recasting it every time it comes off cooldown for the rest of the fight (lowest cooldown and cost, primary contributor to sustained DPS and Dragon Practice stacks).
Basic-attack the dummy in every window between Q/W casts to keep attack speed and on-hit effects contributing.

Cast E only when no other ability needs to be cast during its 1.25s channel, since casting Q, W, or R while E is active ends the channel immediately; let E's automatic bolts finish before weaving the next Q.
Recast W again when it comes off cooldown (~10-14s CD) if the 15s window allows a second cast.
Do not recast R (cooldown far exceeds 15s); treat it as a single opening or mid-fight burst.
questions: Should R be front-loaded at the very start of the fight for maximum total casts across the simulation, or is it more representative to delay it slightly so its cast time doesn't overlap with the opening auto-attack/Q weave?

Given E ends the instant another ability is cast, should the rotation ever interleave E between Q casts, or should E always be scheduled into a gap where no other ability is due for its full 1.25s duration?

Should the rotation assume Smolder opens at 0 Dragon Practice stacks (worst case for a burst-focused sim) or at some pre-built stack count reflecting a realistic mid-fight state, since this changes whether Q ever reaches tier-1/2/3 within the simulated 15s?

Is it correct to assume the dummy is always in range and within Q's unusual target-range mechanic (equal to Smolder's attack range, +100% bonus attack range) for every Q cast, or does itemized attack range change how often Q can be used at range vs. melee-adjacent?
